claim: A neuromorphic silicon-made computer composed of neuron-like elements with cause-effect repertoires similar to those of humans could be conscious.
falsifier: The hypothesis could be tested by constructing a neuromorphic system with the specified properties and assessing whether it exhibits indicators of consciousness (e.g., integrated information measures).

conditions: the system is composed of neuron-like elements
those elements have cause-effect repertoires similar to human ones
exclusions: limited to the hypothesized scenario; empirical confirmation is lacking

title: Composition of neuron-like elements–potential consciousness mechanism

claim: General RL post-training, without additional process annotations or dedicated reward model training, yields per-token scores that aggregate into reliable process-level signals for LLM agents.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by applying the progress advantage computation to any RL-post-trained LLM agent and evaluating the resulting per-token scores on process-level evaluation tasks.

conditions: the RL post-training uses a reference policy as a regularization pivot
the signal is computed from checkpoint pairs (behavior policy and reference policy)
exclusions: limited to the reported experimental settings: five benchmarks, four model families, and three application domains; transfer to other tasks, models, or domains is unestablished

title: RL post-training–effective per-token scores that principle

claim: When a phenomenon cannot be explained by an existing theory, assumptions can be made as the basis of a modeling experiment, and the behavior of the model can be used to evaluate the sufficiency of those assumptions to account for the phenomenon.
falsifier: One can implement this by constructing a model based on specific assumptions for an unexplained phenomenon and comparing its behavior to empirical data to assess sufficiency.

conditions: A phenomenon cannot be readily explained using an existing theory
exclusions: Limited to the reviewed methodology in theoretical neuroscience; transferability to other fields is unestablished.

title: Making assumptions as for Evaluation of the sufficiency
